_about: The publisher's checks (validation.json): the full cosine a check's vector_cosine_at_least is decided on, the JSON pointer a $ref and expect.json.path read with, and the file's grammar. A returned vector is read at its reply's width (float32) and the reference as signed (float64); the cosine is their dot product over both lengths, zero when their lengths differ or either is empty or all zero, and a check passes when the cosine is at least min. A file case says whether the host refuses the package when it reads it (refuse) or reads it (accept), which checks fail, fixed, because a value of theirs does not resolve (unresolved), and which checks are of a lane this host does not run (not_run: read for their name, sets and bound, shown not run, never a refusal); binary_members are members carried as bytes (base64), a session check's recordings; the kit's packer refuses all three kinds. The session lane: normalize is the one normaliser a transcript and a phrase are read with (lowercase, punctuation to space, the apostrophe contractions expanded, a run of digits spelled one digit at a time); levels is a reply's level, the root mean square of every s16le sample in decibels of full scale, 20*log10(rms/32768), null for no level at all; judge is a session check's verdict on what the engine said before its answer was complete: a refused control, an engine failure, the check's own synthesis cancelled or the session ended first is wrong, except a failure saying retry_may_pass, which is timed out; an answer not complete by the check's bound is timed out; then the order (a subsequence of the critical events' types, a withheld final counting for nothing), the transcript (every final's words joined, normalised, each phrase found as consecutive words) and the reply's floor (its samples over its rate in whole milliseconds, its level) decide. The host owns this file (internal/pluginhost/testdata/validation_checks.json); the kit holds a byte copy (vectors/validation_checks.json).
